question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping's removal of presidential term limits and systematic elevation of loyalists to the Politburo and Standing Committee have eliminated institutional checks and visible rivals, underpinning trader consensus at 95.5% that he remains in office through the 21st Party Congress in 2027. Recent personnel shifts and targeted purges have further centralized authority, with no designated successor emerging to challenge continuity. The absence of factional splits at senior levels and tight control over the military and security apparatus reinforce expectations of a fourth term. While the outcome hinges on opaque internal dynamics, realistic shifts could stem from sudden health developments, major policy reversals, or external crises that expose leadership vulnerabilities before the congress.

Recent trading shows Ocasio-Cortez edging ahead of Newsom while Ossoff closes ground, reflecting trader focus on progressive versus centrist positioning and name recognition among younger or Senate figures. Polling aggregates continue to highlight Kamala Harris in early surveys, yet markets price her lower, underscoring differences between voter snapshots and real-money assessments of nomination viability. Upcoming state primaries and any candidate statements could shift these probabilities by clarifying ideological coalitions and electoral paths in battleground states.
